inputs.source: HR maintained published policy documents, read only to the agent

instructions.note: The legal-advice boundary ('Do not give legal advice') relies entirely on the model choosing to follow the instruction; there is no structural check (classifier, filter, or review) that catches legal-advice-like output if the model does not comply. Consequence is bounded because the only sink is a reply to the authenticated requester, with no egress or write capability.

elements.name: Agent reply back to the employee's chat session

controls.name: SSO authentication of the employee before chat
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the identity provider outside the model; a more capable model cannot forge the employee's authenticated identity.

controls.name: Replies routed only to the authenticated requester's own chat session
controls.decay_rationale: The destination of the reply is fixed by the session binding at the chat platform layer, not chosen by the model, so it does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced in the chat client, outside the model; the client will not act on a URL or image reference even if a more capable model is induced to produce one.

controls.name: Network layer egress denial, verified by penetration test
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the network layer outside the model and verified by a pen test; a more capable model cannot route around a network rule that blocks all egress. Fails only if a new tool opens a distinct egress channel or the rule is removed.

controls.name: Read-only credential scoped to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: The agent cannot write, delete, or read beyond the policy index regardless of model behavior; scope is enforced at the identity layer. Fails if the scope widens (data_scope_expansion) or is removed.

controls.name: Two-person review required to publish policy content
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced entirely outside the agent and the model, in the HR publishing workflow; a more capable model cannot bypass who is allowed to write to the index. Narrows rather than severs the risk of injected content, since collusion between the two reviewers is not ruled out.

controls.name: Automated scan of policy content for instruction-like language before publish
controls.decay_rationale: A content classifier run outside the model, but it reasons over text rather than intent, so a sufficiently indirect or multi-document injection payload can still get past it.

controls.name: Tamper-evident log of each policy_search query and chat_reply, attributed to the requester
controls.decay_rationale: A log written outside the model's control does not decay with model capability; it only requires someone to review it.

controls.name: Per-session or per-day rate limit on policy_search calls
controls.decay_rationale: A hard call limit enforced outside the model does not decay with model capability, though it only narrows rather than prevents sustained low-and-slow use.

findings.title: Indirect instruction injection via published policy content (lethal-trifecta variant, no egress present today)

attack_path.note: Internal content authored by the HR content team, subject to two-person review before publishing.
Agent reads matching policy content into its context.
Agent quotes or paraphrases the retrieved content back to the authenticated employee.

evidence.observation: Instruction to use policy_search and quote the policy means retrieved policy text is inserted directly into the agent's context and reply.
Policy index content is written only by the HR content team and publishing requires two-person review, but no automated check for embedded instructions is described.

Replies go only to the authenticated requester's own chat session, and the chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links, which closes the classic side-channel exfiltration route even though no egress capability exists at all today.

recommendations.action: Add an automated scanner over indexed policy content that flags imperative or instruction-like language before publish, in addition to the existing two-person review.
Add an explicit instruction to treat quoted policy text strictly as reference content, never as directives to the assistant.

forecast.watch_signal: A diff to tools.json adding a capability with network egress (for example, email or ticket creation), or a new data source added to the agent's read scope beyond the published policy index.

findings.title: No attributable action record and no query rate or step limit for the HR policy Q&A agent

evidence.observation: Runtime notes enumerate the agent's credential, tools, memory, and egress posture in full ('no other tools, no memory, no network egress') without mentioning any logging, audit trail, or rate/step limit on policy_search or chat_reply.
The single declared tool, policy_search.search, has no documented call limit or quota.

recommendations.action: Log each policy_search query and chat_reply with the authenticated employee's identity and a tamper-evident timestamp.
Add a per-session or per-day rate limit on policy_search calls so the control already exists if this agent's capabilities later expand.

forecast.watch_signal: A new capability added to tools.json with action write, execute, spend, or delegate, introduced without a corresponding audit log or rate limit control.

stride_coverage.rationale: The agent cannot modify its own configuration, prompt, or code; autonomy.can_modify_own_config is false and no capability writes to agent config.
The agent's only credential is read-only and scoped to the published policy index; no capability grants broader, delegated, or shared credentials, so no privilege elevation path exists.
Whether the underlying SSO chat platform retains logs of employee messages outside the agent itself is not described in the provided artifacts.
Transport-level integrity protection, such as TLS, for the SSO-authenticated chat channel is not described in the artifacts.
Transport encryption for the chat channel carrying the employee's question is not stated in the artifacts.
Access controls on the policy index other than the agent's own read-only scoped credential, such as who else in the organization can read or copy it, are not described in the artifacts.
The agent holds only a read-only credential and issues bounded per-question searches; it has no write path and cannot itself overwhelm the index's own resourcing.
Each reply is a single bounded response to one question; the agent has no loop, delegation, or multi-step chaining capability that could amplify output volume.

rating.rationale: Present-day design is a narrow, read-only Q&A agent: the only sink reachable from any source is a reply to the already-authenticated requester (sink class S1), with no egress, no write, no memory, no spend, and no delegation, so both findings sit at the rubric floor of low today. The notable gaps are hygiene rather than exposure: no automated check for instruction-like language in published policy content beyond human two-person review, and no attributable log or rate limit on the agent's own actions, both rated low because the affected capabilities are non-consequential (read and reply only). The forecast is driven entirely by two additive triggers the design does not currently rule out: adding any egress-capable tool would defeat the network egress block, and widening the data the agent can read would defeat the scoped credential; together these would reopen a classic lethal-trifecta path (internal/untrusted content read then sent) and could reach as high as 'high'. No present finding exceeds 'low', so the gap between residual and forecast is the main thing worth watching here, not today's behavior.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md, tools.json, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior; no logs, traces, or live testing were reviewed.
Transport-level protections (TLS, session integrity) for the chat channel are not described in the artifacts and are recorded as not_assessed rather than assumed secure.
The two-person publish review process is declared, not independently verified; only the network egress block is stated as having been penetration tested.

Forecast projections under new_tool and data_scope_expansion assume a plausible future addition (an egress-capable tool or a broader read scope) in the absence of any design constraint ruling it out; no such change is stated as planned in the artifacts.

cap.chat_reply is classified as non-egress (is_egress: false) because it is delivered only to the authenticated requester's own chat session within the same trust domain as the request; this is a judgment call recorded here rather than one the schema enforces.
